The template is not invoked by importing this module.

## B1 whitelist and fail-fast order

B1 has six distinct `/proc` paths. The first remote-process operation in any future reviewed implementation must read only the boot ID as an ordinary user:

`/proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id`

The first bytes must match the historical authorization baseline `822a9c29-37c0-438c-81c4-da998d57073b`. If they do not match, the process exits immediately; it must not open any of the other five paths. If the boot ID matches, the only remaining B1 paths are:

| Order | Path | Limit | Rule |
|---|---|---:|---|
| 1 | `/proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id` | 1 MiB | First read; exact expected boot required before any other path |
| 2 | `/proc/sys/kernel/osrelease` | 1 MiB | One read |
| 3 | `/proc/version` | 1 MiB | One read |
| 4 | `/proc/cmdline` | 1 MiB | One read |
| 5 | `/proc/uptime` | 1 MiB | One read |
| 6 | `/proc/self/mountinfo` | 1 MiB | One read; descriptive evidence only |

After those five reads, the future process must reread `boot_id` and stop if it differs from the first bytes. A read error, including `EACCES`, stops the process at that point. There is no retry, privilege change, alternative path, or fallback. These are six distinct files and at most seven read operations when the start/end boot-ID checks are included.

The process must use ordinary-user permissions for every path. The command template must not invoke `sudo` or another elevation method. `EACCES` is a terminal rejection; it must not trigger a prompt, PAM authentication, `auth.log` activity caused by elevation, or a second command.

## B2 file and mount contract

B2 is a separately reviewed stage, after B1 evidence is assessed. A future B2 process must also check the same boot ID before opening `/boot` and recheck it after the file transaction. B2 adds only the regular file `/boot/BOOT.BIN`; it must not use `mountinfo` text as the sole read-only check.

The required directory-relative sequence is:

```python
dir_fd = os.open("/boot", os.O_RDONLY | os.O_DIRECTORY | os.O_NOFOLLOW)
fd = os.open("BOOT.BIN", os.O_RDONLY | os.O_NOFOLLOW, dir_fd=dir_fd)
```

Before reading any file-content byte, call `os.fstatvfs(fd)` and require `bool(f_flag & os.ST_RDONLY)`, then capture `os.fstat(fd)`. Read the file through that pinned descriptor. Immediately after the content read, call `os.fstatvfs(fd)` again and require `ST_RDONLY`, then call `os.fstat(fd)` again. The pre-read and post-read tuples `(st_dev, st_ino, st_size, st_mtime_ns)` must match exactly. Close both descriptors on every path.

Any symlink rejection, non-regular object, missing flag, writable filesystem, changed stat tuple, changed boot ID, `EACCES`, or I/O error stops the stage. In particular, a writable `fstatvfs` result before the content read requires zero content reads. Do not retry, remount, mount, unmount, change flags, try another path, or escalate privileges. `O_NOATIME` is not a fallback for the `ST_RDONLY` requirement.

`ST_RDONLY` is the required kernel VFS assertion for the filesystem containing the opened target file at the two check points. This establishes **目标文件/挂载点只读** for the target and those check points. It does not establish **整张 SD 卡零写入**: an SSH login can still cause system logging or other activity. If whole-card zero-write is required, keep the card offline and do not use SSH.

## SSH and interpreter option whitelist

If a later, separately approved stage is ever prepared, its SSH option set must include all of the following:

| Option | Required value | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `-T` | enabled | No pseudo-terminal |
| `-o ControlMaster=no` | fixed | No multiplexed control connection |
| `-o ClearAllForwardings=yes` | fixed | Clear configured port, agent, and X11 forwarding |
| `-o StrictHostKeyChecking=yes` | fixed | Reject unknown or changed host keys |
| `-o UserKnownHostsFile=C:/Users/POP/.ssh/wo0015-known_hosts` | fixed absolute path | Use one explicitly named host-key file |

The existence and contents of the proposed host-key file, target identity, and current SSH reachability were not inspected or verified here. This work does not create or modify that file or any global SSH file. Historical host-pin evidence remains untouched and must be identified and reviewed separately; do not use `accept-new`, `ssh-keyscan`, or another automatic trust-creation path. A missing/untrusted key must fail closed; do not accept a key interactively or switch to another known-hosts file. No host, username, key, address, or connection command is supplied in this proposal.

The remote interpreter flags are fixed as `-I -S -B`. The executable path and presence on a future target remain unverified and must be reviewed before any later approval. No `sudo`, PTY, ControlMaster, forwarding, retry, or fallback command is part of this proposal.

## Command disposition and evidence boundary

The earlier v1 command document included a noninteractive `sudo` wrapper. That v1 command is superseded for any future consideration and must not be copied into a new request. The old files remain unchanged as historical evidence. This v2 document describes policy and syscall order only; it does not implement or invoke them.

Offline tests use synthetic bytes and in-memory mock methods only. They do not open `/proc` or `/boot`, create a real SSH process, call a remote backend, or grant AFI/DMA authorization. Current status remains `STOPPED_PRECONDITION_UNVERIFIED` and `afi_authorized=false`.
